mutant_policy: Every serialized descriptor path with a recorded non-default witness has one exact field/case/observation entry in field_mutants. Each mutation skips only that assignment while consuming its wire bytes, proves the target retained poison immediately after successful public load, and runs an unmutated control. Compare run result, every PCM sample, frames and metadata, battery and RTC projection, rumble line, observer deltas, post-load canonical save, and final canonical bytes; require every declared discrepancy. A path whose guest-visible effect is refreshed before the next sample, such as div from divider_counter, uses the explicit immediate public load/save canonical-byte discrepancy and still runs the later output comparison. Only the three explicitly reasoned input_events component mutants may stop at a rejected post-load canonical save; all other successful target saves must reach both future slices. Timeout, crash, setup, load, and generic failures are not semantic kills.

field_mutants.observation_rationale: At the accepted_dma_phase DMG cut, omitting the sample phase changes the two bounded PCM slices and final canonical bytes; the run-result remains equal.
At the apu_fields CGB cut, the omitted sample buffer changes bounded PCM; it is consumed and reconverges before the final state comparison, so final canonical bytes remain equal.

field_mutants.malformed_target_reason: The div_read DMG seed ties div=0xAC to divider_counter=0xAC00, and the state invariant requires div to equal the counter high byte; omitting div therefore causes canonical save rejection.

field_mutants.observation_rationale: At the key1_switch CGB speed-switch stall cut, omitting double_speed changes the future run result and final canonical state; the two bounded PCM slices remain equal.
At the visible-demo cut, omission changes frame completion metadata in the bounded continuation; the later frame completion normalizes this field, so final canonical bytes match.

At the apu_fields CGB cut, omission changes the frame completion metadata observed in the bounded continuation; the timing field is normalized before the final canonical save, so final bytes remain equal.

field_mutants.malformed_target_reason: The native_pipeline_hdma CGB cut is mid-byte with nonzero HDMA byte phase; the accepted-state invariant requires an active transfer for that phase, so omitting hdma.active causes canonical save rejection.

The accepted_dma_phase DMG cut has a nonzero queued event in slot zero; the state invariant requires unused event slots to be zero, so omitting input_event_count makes the receiver invalid and canonical save rejects it.
Skipping the active event timestamp makes it precede the saved machine clock; the runner stops after canonical save rejection.
Skipping the active event kind violates the public state validator's event-kind/value relation; the runner stops after canonical save rejection.
Skipping the active event value leaves the kind/value pair outside the public state validator's accepted relation; the runner stops after canonical save rejection.

field_mutants.observation_rationale: At the apu_fields DMG cut, omission changes immediate canonical bytes; the guest consumes or replaces the flag before the measured future outputs, so run results, PCM, frame metadata and final bytes match.
At the dmg_ppu_pipeline DMG cut, omission changes immediate canonical bytes; the selected-object count is consumed before later bounded output and final state observations, which match.
At the apu_fields CGB cut, omission changes frame data and metadata during the bounded continuation; later PPU output reconverges, so final canonical bytes match.

field_mutants.malformed_target_reason: At the bus_unsupported CGB cut, serial_control=0x80 denotes an active external transfer; clearing serial_active while leaving that restored control bit set violates the serial relation, so canonical save rejects the omitted target.

At the bus_unsupported CGB cut, an active external serial transfer has serial_control=0x80 and zero edge countdown; any distinct legal single-field control value breaks the active/control/countdown invariant, so canonical save rejects the omitted target.

At the native_pipeline CGB cut, wram_bank is greater than one and the accepted-state invariant requires it to equal SVBK; raw SVBK zero only aliases effective bank one, so no distinct valid SVBK value exists and canonical save rejects the omitted target.

At the timer_reload CGB cut, divider_counter=0x005C and timer_signal=1; TAC value 5 is the only accepted selector in this fixture whose enabled tap is high, so omitting tac causes canonical save rejection.

At the timer_reload CGB cut, timer_reload_remaining is four; the accepted-state invariant requires a pending reload whenever remaining is nonzero, so omitting timer_reload_pending causes canonical save rejection.

field_mutants.observation_rationale: At the timer_reload CGB cut, the omitted remaining count changes immediate canonical bytes; the pending reload resolves before guest output diverges, so bounded run results, PCM, frame metadata and final canonical bytes match.

field_mutants.malformed_target_reason: At the timer_reload CGB cut, TAC=5 and divider_counter=0x005C derive timer_signal=1; omitting the derived signal breaks that accepted-state invariant, so canonical save rejects the target.

At the native_pipeline CGB cut, the effective WRAM bank is derived from the restored SVBK value; the accepted-state invariant requires wram_bank=(svbk==0 ? 1 : svbk), so omitting the cache assignment causes canonical save rejection.
